utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to apologise for the delay. Judge Szenasi is not feeling well this morning so the remaining Judges, according to Rule 15(B) decided to continue our proceedings today. And this afternoon, we will have an extra sitting. Originally it was set at 4:00 but I believe that the initial appearance in another case will not last that long, so we might start a little bit early, for instance 3:30 until 5:00, if the courtroom permits us. Well, having said that, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karavelic, yesterday I was showing you the order from Sefer Halilovic, that was P161, of the 2nd of September 1993, asking for the delta unit parts of the 9th and 10th Brigade and -- and then Solakovic's unit. What was your response to receiving that order from Sefer Halilovic? Firstly, do you need to see it again on the screen or do you remember it sufficiently?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it. There is no need to put it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your response to receiving the order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say anything in particular about what the reaction was. It was within the range of a normal reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What, yours or Mr. Halilovic's?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reaction. I'm thinking of myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the moment when I received the order, the last one that we were looking at yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not the very moment, but what did you do in response to receiving it? Did you act on it? Did you -- did you obey it? Did you refuse to obey it? Did you contact someone? Did you contact Mr. Halilovic? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember doing anything in particular. I think I got in touch with Rasim Delic who also confirmed that I should act in accordance with Sefer Halilovic's order and then after that, I started to implement the order of the Chief of Staff of the main -- the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you contact Rasim Delic after having received Mr. Halilovic's order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simply because of a basic military rule. The commander of the Main Staff is a superior to the corps commander, and that is one of the main reasons why I got in touch with General Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic was your superior in -- was senior to you in the Bosnian army. Why did you feel it necessary to contact General Delic after having received -- you having received an order from someone who was senior to you in the army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was quite specific in my previous answer, if we understand what military hierarchy means, and what command and control means, and what the chain of command means.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what was it about receiving an order from Mr. Halilovic, who was the Chief of the Main Staff that caused you to contact Rasim Delic to seek his confirmation of that order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you would like me to say anything more, well, I can say that at that point in time, I did not have access to the order which I only saw once I came to The Hague, which General -- in which General Delic named Sefer Halilovic as the head of the team to carry out certain tasks in the Neretva River valley to do some things relating to the 4th and the 6th corps. This was an order of the 30th of August. At that point in time I was not quite sure why I was supposed to send units to the Neretva River valley and this is the reason why I contacted Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen a copy of the order of the 30th of August at the time, would you have sent the troops without contacting Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's an objection because of a speculative question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. It's a hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw the question in that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I just want you to clarify something from your last answer in which you said that you saw that order when you came to The Hague. Would seeing that order in 1993 have made any difference to whether or not you would have called Rasim Delic in the normal course of your response to receiving such an order from Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's exactly the same question just twice as long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm pressing the question because the witness has given an answer in which he has alluded to the fact that seeing that order may have made some difference. I'm attempting to clarify whether that order if he had seen that order it would have made any difference to whether or not he felt the need to contact Rasim Delic. That is if that order standing alone, if he'd had access to it, would have conveyed information to him that he didn't need to get from Rasim Delic. It goes to the whole question of subordination and where Mr. Halilovic fitted in and why the witness felt the need to contact Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe the final aim is justified, but this question actually is not proper one because it's asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is it any more speculating than if you asked a witness, "If you received this order from your commander, what should your response have been?" "Within the normal military chain -- within the normal military doctrine, that is had you seen this order appointing Mr. Halilovic as head of the team, would you have needed to" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: My suggestion is that you may ask a general question without mentioning that particular order, just as a normal, routine practice in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, in terms of your experience and knowledge of military doctrine and subordination within the Bosnian army, if a -- if the commander, supreme commander, appoints a certain officer as -- to lead a team allowing certain things, what would your response be -- what is the normal response of someone in your position to seeing such an order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a very often used rule. It existed in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and I believe that it exists in most of the world armies. When a commander issues an order to a commander, a superior to his lower-ranking officer, then there is no need to comment or double check or anything like that. However, very often, we have a situation in which specifically in the staff of the supreme -- in the Supreme Command staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, some orders or types of documents were issued by a deputy, Jovo Divjak, that was one deputy, or the other deputy Stjepan Siber, and they issued also -- the chiefs of the administrations of the Supreme Command staff also issued all kinds of instructions, orders, and so on. All such orders which were issued by members of the Supreme Command Staff are issued in the name of the commander. It was quite often the case that the corps commanders, when such documents would arrive from officers or generals who were members of that staff, would check and ask the commander, specifically we're talking about Mr. Rasim Delic in this case, is this so and so, are you backing this particular order? Has this been coordinated or not, depending on the matter involved, because the commander of the Supreme Command staff is a superior to all the corps commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do -- when you spoke to Mr. Delic, did he tell you what Mr. Halilovic was doing, and why he wanted those particular troops?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember the whole conversation, but the gist of it was that, yes, I should act according to the orders and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown the next document which is 65 ter number 40, 01831484?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 382.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a document dated the 2nd of September, an order from Mr. Halilovic, or a request, to the 1st Corps Command, personally to the commander. Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were many documents, perhaps I did and perhaps I did not, but most likely I did see it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The time stamp on this one is -- I'm sorry, can you tell me when your corps received it? I think if you look in the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states here, Sarajevo, the date and the time, the 3rd of September, so it was in the night between the 2nd and the 3rd, at 1 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It says that "We request that you send an urgent response regarding the order for your units to move into the Neretva valley, indicate when a unit will move, and state its numerical strength so that its reception and transport can be organised." What was your response to this?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all the contacts after that talked about the fact that preparations of my units were underway and that -- date and the time when the units would move out. So to carry out all the preparations and make it possible for the units to move out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I move to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours this one raises an interesting question of the way that Your Honours admit these documents because, although the witness hasn't said that he specifically saw it, frankly, he would have seen thousands of documents and he can't be expected to remember each one. It seems to have been addressed to his corps and there seems to be a sensible basis on which one can infer that it would have passed through his hands and been seen. Therefore, although he doesn't remember specifically seeing it, in this case, this is different to some of the other orders and some of the other documents that have come along where the people say "I know nothing about it at all." So it's really a matter for the Tribunal but I would say the Defence doesn't strongly oppose its being admitted because it's likely that he saw it so the Defence doesn't oppose its admission but it remains a matter for Your Honour of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. I believe that your position is very reasonable. So this document is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution exhibit P382.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Having received those two -- the order and the request from Mr. Halilovic, did you in fact order the soldiers he specified the Delta Brigade the 2nd Independent Battalion and parts of the 9th and the 10th, did you in fact order them to go to Bradina in accordance with the order of the 2nd of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the order from the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, and also based on an order which came later from the chief dated the 20th of September, when he also asked for more units, without actually naming the specific units, I issued many orders to these units of mine that went there and that were supposed to go there but did not actually go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit 65 ter 43, 00585512?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI 383.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While that document is coming, were the orders you issued to the subordinate units in writing or oral?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both oral and written orders have the same weight. My rule, as a military man, is to try to issue written orders and also to ask for such orders from my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have a look at the document on the screen, MFI 383. It's an order under -- with your name on it and your signature, of the 4th of September 1993, addressed to the motorised brigade, to Ramiz Delalic in person. Is that an order which you issued on the 4th of September 1993 to Ramiz Delalic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, unless I'm mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you issue that -- was that an order you issued in response to Mr. Halilovic's order to you, confirmed by Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is stated in the first paragraph, in the introductory paragraph of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The first part of the order says, you order, one, the immediate formation of a company of 50 soldiers, that's two platoons of 25 soldiers each, all organisational preparations shall be undertaken and the company shall be ready to move towards Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours the translation that I have says that the -- that the order says "immediately select men for a 50-strong company." It doesn't suggest the formation of a company at all, which may be technically quite a different thing. So I don't know if my friend has got a different translation than I have, but the actual words ought to be used if it's being put in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at first glance, there is no major differences between the two translations, but, however, we are doing a specific work here so I believe that the translation issue is important. So would you please allow the Prosecution to proceed and after this seeking we will entrust the translation office to check the translation of this document. Of course, during your cross-examination, you may use your own version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just say Your Honours I certainly am far from wanting to start another difficulty on that topic, and it may simply be a translation problem. The witness himself, because he's got the original document there, he can comment on what is said there better than perhaps I can with my English translation. So I just alert the Tribunal to the fact that I've got a different one. Anyway I've done what I have to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I inquire whether Mr. Morrissey has an interpretation, a translation which the Defence have obtained or a draft? The one I'm reading from is the final translation. That may solve it. If he has the draft one, that may solve it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, but first of all you may ask the witness himself to read the first sentence, to see what his understanding of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour there is no issue about it. As Your Honour pointed out, whether it's immediate, and if it's translated there had way it's not going to be a proper translation, it's going to be an interpretation. So we won't get it precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. We quite understand that. But that's a request put by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If I can remember where I was -- excuse me for a moment. Just go to paragraph 1 of that order, Mr. Karavelic. Relating to the translation I have it says the immediate formation. I'm not so much interested in the word "immediate." I'm more interested in why you asked or why you ordered a company of 50 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to that question is very complex for a number of reasons. When a small number of men from a larger unit is requested, as is the case here, it is impossible very often to ask the brigade commander to allocate an establishment company or a platoon, depending on the way the work is organised in his area of responsibility, in terms of maintaining the line of defence. If a company is divided into three parts, a third maintaining the line, a third is resting, and a third is in reserve, or actually a third is resting at home, it's difficult to disrupt this organisation with requests. So very often we would just instruct the brigade commander that such and such a number of men is required and to organise a certain number of men who know each other anyway in order that a certain task can be carried out. However as a soldier I have to admit that the best way to do it is to send establishment units to implement tasks. However, this was not always possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you by that order intending Mr. Delalic to select the men himself?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably before I drafted the order, I talked to the brigade commander. Sulejman Imsirevic, and I can't be quite sure about it, but I seem to vaguely recall that Sulejman Imsirevic said that Ramiz Delalic would be responsible for that unit that would be sent to implement that particular task. And this is why my officers who drafted this order -- I didn't draft it myself but I signed it, and I stand by it -- addressed it to Ramiz Delalic as deputy commander of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Within the normal military hierarchy, or chain of command, was it normal for you as the corps commander to send an order -- such an order addressed personally to the deputy commander of a subordinate unit?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, you need to pay attention that the first line states "command of the 9th Motorised Brigade." The command, to the command. And that command includes all of its organs headed by the commander, along with the previous answer that I gave, it only formally states "for Ramiz Delalic, personally," because he was probably entrusted by the commander to carry out that task. A commander has much broader duties and tasks. We are talking here about 50 if fighters but his brigade numbered probably about 4.000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay, but in terms of the normal military hierarchy, was it a normal practice for a corps commander such as you to send such an order noted on it to Ramiz Delalic as a deputy commander in person?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All my deputies in the command of the 1st Corps, the assistant for legal affairs, for morale, for logistics, for finance, the Chief of Staff et cetera et cetera, they, when they were drafting their documents, they would prepare those documents and then bring them to me as the corps commander for my signature, and I would sign the original just like this document that I signed, and then they would address these documents to their people according to the vertical line. For instance, if an assistant for legal affairs made such a document, he would then address it to the other counterpart, the 9th Motorised Brigade, the deputy for legal affairs, and I would sign it as the corps commander. So this is the military rule and it does not -- it is not in breach of the rules of service in any way whatsoever or of the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where is Bradina, which is referred to in the first order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere midway between Sarajevo and Jablanica, or perhaps a bit closer to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What -- was it your understanding that Ramiz Delalic was to accompany that company to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be specific about that. His brigade commander knew that actually he was the one who knew that, whether he had actually assigned him to that task or not. I don't know whether he was there in the Neretva River valley all that time with the unit. It is quite possible that he had permission from his brigade commander for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he have your permission to go to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you I didn't give any permissions to Ramiz Delalic or not. It was his brigade commander. He was his deputy. He was not my deputy. So his assignment to any task would be decided by his brigade commander. I made a decisions when it came to the departure of brigade commanders and that is the basic difference, and that is a strict military rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did it require your permission for brigade commanders to leave Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I just said. My previous replies in answer to this question that you just put me. But this only applied to the brigade commanders, to the next lowest in ranks -- in rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I move to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P383.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now that's an issue -- P383 is an order you issued to Ramiz Delalic in person. Did you also issue orders, similar orders, to the 2nd Independent Brigade, the Delta Brigade, and the 10th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I also answered this question in one of my previous answers. The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And again, in case we missed something, was it -- were the orders issued in writing, sorry, did you issue the orders in writing to those subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often, it was -- they were in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we please move to 65 ter number 42, 02122410?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 384.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Having issued those orders, the written orders to the four subordinate units, did you respond to Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to make it clear when we talk about these four units, I'm not sure whether up to that point, the Delta Brigade was subordinated to me. We should -- we would need to check the documents. I really cannot recall it myself. I'm not quite sure whether it was an organic component of the 1st Corps at that time or not. That needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you respond to Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did. I replied to him on a number of occasions in my documents. I'm not quite sure what document you are referring to or what particular instance you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Hopefully there should be one on the screen now dated the 4th of September 1993, order 5/10-48, under your hand, addressed to Mr. Halilovic, chief of the Supreme Command, personally, and Vehbija Karic in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a response that you sent to Mr. Halilovic on the 4th of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite probably. This particular document does not mean anything much to me because these are minor things. I see the document. It is quite possible that it is. If it is a valid document, it means that it is such a response.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 1 which says "between 180" -- sorry, "between 160 and 180 troops will be ready this evening at 2200 hours on 4th of September, 1993, in accordance with your order which we have received." Where did you receive the information from that there were -- that you had that number of troops ready to go?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, these are questions that are beyond any conceivable -- where did I get them from? My inferiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The second part of the order says that "the troops should report to Nedzad Nadzic or Salko Muminovic at the IKM on Igman, 2200 hours." Was that -- was that particular piece of information related to the earlier order, part 3 of the earlier order in which you said they were going to Igman? Is that a way of informing Mr. Halilovic that that was what was happening?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That precisely can be seen from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I move to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is in the same category as that other order. He can't remember it but he probably dealt with it. We don't object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P384.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did those soldiers in fact leave that night? That was the night in which the order or the response indicates they were ready to go. That's the 4th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the four years of the war, I extracted from Sarajevo perhaps over 100.000, 100.000 soldiers. What I'm saying is that some of them actually came in and went out four or five times from the city. So to remember all these details in such a huge machinery, where the commander is just a cog in this organisation, the kind of organisational work that you have in a corps formation which has 75.000 people is just a person who approves different actions and requires of his men to be conscientious and responsible and not to actually create any situations that would push him beyond the law or to act in contravention of the rules of service. So it is hard for me to remember all these details at this point. If this is the first such departure, and I believe that it is, I believe that we had certain problems with the units sitting out because of the inclement weather. As far as I can remember, from what I read in another document, I believe that on that occasion, it was postponed by 24 hours on account of the bad weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Well, that's actually the shorthand way of answering that, and can you please, please, answer in the shorthand way? We will be here for a long time if you don't. I'm going to show that document now.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise but I do not want -- I would not like to be misunderstood. Four years of warfare and you're asking me whether on a specific night 50 or a different number of people left the town, but I'm telling you that I sent hundreds and thousands of men through Igman, through Mount Igman, for days in and out, throughout the four years, and you're asking me about a specific night. I cannot remember. I just want to make that point. Because I don't want the Court to draw a mistaken conclusion from what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The proceeding in this Court, Witness, is that you have to answer the questions put to you by the parties. If you are not sure about the answer, you may simply say "No, I don't remember." If the Prosecution needs some explanations, he will ask you the follow-up questions. And we also will give you the opportunity to explain your answer, if you feel you need to do so. However, it is -- the party asking the questions leads you through those evidence. Gentlemen, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P290? Is it on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic can you please look at P290? You referred a moment ago to seeing a document. I think you'll find this document bears your name. It's dated the 5th of September 1993. It's addressed to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, Jablanica, to Sefer Halilovic personally. Now, does that assist with your recollection of whether or not the soldiers left on the night of the 4th of September, which was referred to in the previous order, or information, that is Exhibit P384?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I cannot recall with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Is this an order which was sent under your hand?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is a valid document, there is no signature here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the first part of the document. It's addressed to Mr. Halilovic. And it says personally. And in Jablanica. Was it your understanding that that's where he was at that time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not mine as the inferior officer to know where my superior is. That is a strict military rule. I received my documents from Jablanica and I sent documents to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, the heading is, "in connection with your order, confidential, 015363-1-2/93 of the 2nd of September 1993 from Jablanica, I hereby forward a response." The document bearing that number was P383 which was the order of the 4th of September 1993. I'm sorry, which was the order of the 2nd of September 1993. Let's go to the first part, paragraph 1, "At 2200 hours last night, 4/5 September 1993, a company from the 10th, 130 soldiers, and a company from the 9th, 60 soldiers were, ready for the task in question. All organisational material preparations with these units had been completed. At 2230 hours, when the vehicles arrived due to a major storm Caco and Celo personally proposed to me that the departure be postponed for 24 hours. However, after that in the course of the day today it was put off completely. I am aware of the overall situation in a your area in the zone of the 4th and 6th corps [unfortunately such are the circumstances]." Now, does that information recorded there accord with your recollection of what happened? Was there a storm which delayed the departure of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Celo and Caco personally propose to you that the departure be postponed for 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "personally"?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does the document in Bosnian say something different to personal? I'm just relying on the translation I have. Please look at it.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see the document very well. Especially if I wrote it, and it does say personally. But are you asking me whether they actually did personally propose to me that this be done? So I'm asking you what do you mean by that personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe there is a confusion. Did they propose to you, impersonally or personally, that the departure be postponed for 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may be allowed a minute more, we are now sitting here 12 years after the fact in this nice room. 12 years after.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you go on, please be aware we do have an understanding that it's a long time ago and as His Honour Judge Liu said, if you don't remember --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't understand me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm trying to focus your answers to the questions I'm asking you. If you don't remember or you're not sure, please just tell us.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document would normally be prepared by my staff, and my officers from my staff actually drafted this document. I as the corps commander did not draft documents. That is why what the command and the -- of a hundred people and the whole staff were there for. And they put that there, that Caco and Celo had personally proposed this. Now, who talked to them, it is possible that I did myself. I do not remember that. Perhaps it was my assistants, the officers who drafted this document that talked to them. And they proposed saying that the weather was bad during that night, that we should not send the people there because of the possible consequences and so on and so forth. This is why I asked you why you -- what do you mean by "personally"? Because you're asking me a very direct and concrete question. I can tell you I don't know, I don't remember, I didn't see, but that is not what I want to do because I respect this Court. I want to be as precise as possible, as clear as possible, but my just responding, I don't know, I haven't -- I didn't hear it or something to that effect, I am not clear enough and not precise enough in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It is perfectly clear now. Move to the next part. "However, after that, in the course of the day today, it was put off completely." Is that correct? There was a storm and it was put off, it was postponed and then put off? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably. The way -- the way it is written in the document, I myself do not remember that at all, that particular day, I cannot recall that particular day at this point in time, today.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you please look at the stamp on the document? Does that indicate to you that the document was sent and received in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stamp that we can see is the stamp of the communications centre service, which, through communication parcels were -- would send or dispatch or receive documents. So this is just a stamp which attests to the fact that a document had been sent, i.e. received, as indicated, i.e., as addressed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you please move now to document P116. Have you seen this document before coming to The Hague? That's a document dated the 6th of September -- I'm sorry, the 5th of September 1993, from the Jablanica IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, just before we get to that matter, I'm -- I -- I might have missed it. Did my learned friend seek to tender the previous document or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that the previous document is admitted already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The question is: Have you -- had you seen that document, P116, before you came to The Hague to testify?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you see it before coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the archives of the federation army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 1, it's addressed to Sefer Halilovic personally, and purportedly from SVK members, Amidza, Rifat, and Zicko -- paragraph 1 says, "We received a reply from Vaha, explaining that they will not be able to send any soldiers due to recent developments. Sefer, we need to find and pull out other soldiers from Sarajevo because we cannot do the job without a reserve of 200 soldiers." Were -- do you believe that you're the Vaha in question referred to in that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours I'm sorry to interrupt again here I've got a different document on the screen. I know what's happened, I think, here, but the English translation that my learned friend read out is quite different to what I've got and it's not a different translation. I think it's actually a different but similar document. There are two documents very like this in existence, and I think my friend has read out one and what's on the screen on my computer now, I'm guessing, is the other one. We are not suggesting any sinister plot here; I think it's just a confusion. But I think I better point that out because the one I've got doesn't mention the figure "200 soldiers." I don't know what -- which one Your Honours have got on the screen there or which one the Prosecutors have got on their screen, frankly. There is such a document, I'm very familiar with what my learned friend read out, and I think it's on another similar piece of correspondence. But we just better make sure we are all looking at the right one before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you tell us what's the number of the other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It -- it -- it hasn't been admitted yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We've got an internal Defence numbering system of it, but I don't know if that would help the -- the Prosecutors in any way. There -- there are two on the same day. I think the Prosecutors have better find it. So far as I can help, I know there are two sent by the same Amidza, Rifat, and it might be inferred that's Karic, Belajic [phoen], and Suljevic. And that they sent two letters addressed to Sefer Halilovic in Sarajevo concerning the news that they got from this witness. So that's what I think it is. And I think the Prosecutors might have both or might have -- but anyway the one on the screen is one and he -- I don't think my friend's read from the other one. So we better just make sure we've got the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My learned friend Mr. Morrissey is entirely correct. I had stapled the wrong English translation to the -- I just switched them. I apologise, Mr. Karavelic and to the Court, I should actually be reading the English translation which says, "We have been informed by Vaha that he won't be sending us the troops that we were -- that were deployed to Hrasnica. We -- he promised that he would send us a more detailed explanation as to the reason for this decision but we haven't received any as yet." It's the same question: Do you believe that you're the Vaha in question being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my document. This is a document that the three persons who signed it, and in which they are sending this information to Sefer Halilovic. How they acquired this information is known only to them. They did call me Vaha often so I assume that it is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you had in fact sent them some information saying you wouldn't -- the troops wouldn't be arriving that night, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't believe so. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think we just did that a few moments ago, looked at a document you sent saying that the troops weren't coming because of the storm.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then that's it. I thought that you meant something else, just now, when you put the question to me. That is that document. It's a document dated the 5th, and this document here is dated the 6th. So in the first document, it says that they are not going to send anything, and that's how I understand this document, that they will not send anything. That's why I gave you the answer that I'm not sure whether I ever said that I would not send them the units. However, the document of the 1st states why the departure time was delayed, of the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know of anyone else in Sarajevo called Vaha who was sending troops to the forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is two things to raise there. I'd object to cross-examining of this witness firstly, but secondly I don't think it's it maybe a controversy about nothing. I don't think the witness is contesting what's being said and I can indicate I'm not going to oppose the tendering of this document, so my friend may not need to go through these steps if he -- if he chooses not to. But in any event I submit there shouldn't be cross-examining of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But at least we have to know the answer from this witness, who is the Vaha mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If it needs to be clarified, then I say no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's just a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is was there anyone else you know of called Vaha in Sarajevo who was sending troops to the forward command post -- or at the direction of the forward command post in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at the transcript in my previous answer I answered this, that probably it is me. The question is repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P122?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry just before we get to that one, is that previous document going to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe they are already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The previous one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies. I apologise. I've done that twice now and I'm just making sure. I've got a list which I thought was -- my apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: P122, is it on the screen there? It's an order of the 6th of September 1993 from Mr. Halilovic. Now, have you -- had you seen that document before you came to The Hague to testify?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I saw this document for the first time when I was giving you my third statement in Sarajevo at your offices in Nedzarici. This was about a year and a half or two years ago. I did not see this document during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While we are with this document, I want to ask you about subordination. The order from Mr. Halilovic, P161, the order of the 2nd of September, ordered you to send the soldiers to Bradina where the 1st Corps command would take them over. In military subordination terms, what did that mean about who was in control or command of the troops from the time they left Sarajevo until they got to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you made a lapse when you said that they should be taken over by the 1st Corps. I think it's supposed to be the 4th Corps in Gradina -- Bradina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are actually both wrong. It was actually the 6th, sorry. But what was the effect of that -- of that order in terms of the subordination? Who was in command and control of the troops from when they left Sarajevo to when they got to Bradina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific case, I had the authority to command and control. This was my chain of command. It's important to say my chain of command. I did not directly command these companies, these two companies. On the other hand, I did have command and control in accordance with the chain of command. So as the corps commander, I did have command from the top down, and as such, I had the authority of control and command over these companies up until the point in time when they arrived at their destination and reported to the Supreme Command group which was headed by General Sefer Halilovic. After that, the chain of command which functioned, which was established, in the course of the implementation of the Neretva-93 operation, this chain of command had command and control over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when did you receive command and control back over those particular soldiers who went to Herzegovina? What I mean is, when were they back under your subordination? At what point?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On their return to their home unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mean to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be, but it could be at another point where the units were handed over. It could have been in Bradina, it could have been in Sarajevo, in Jablanica. It depends on the way the order is regulated. But let's say that it would be Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We started at 9.20. Do Your Honours want -- wish me to continue? It's an hour and ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm entirely in your hands. If you finished with this document, we might have a break but if you did not, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll continue with the document, then, general.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've just told us that from the -- that Mr. Halilovic's chain of command -- chain of command had command and control over those soldiers once they reached their destination and reported to the Supreme Command group headed by Mr. Halilovic. I want you to have a look at this document, and the paragraph that says, "units from the 1st" -- "units from the 1st" -- I withdraw that. The first paragraph, it says, "With regard to previous 6th corps units tasked combat operations in the 4th Corps zone of responsibility and the engagement of the Zulfikar Reconnaissance Sabotage Brigade on the axis Vrdi village, Goranci village towards Mostar, the following units are," I think it says "resubordinated," "to this brigade, Dreznica Battalion and units from the 1st Corps." Now, what is the meaning of that in military terms?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment, before that is dealt with, Your Honours, there is an -- I've got a complaint to make here. My learned friend took the witness back to commenting on a previous order. That was the order back -- which directed the troops to go to Bradina. And be taken over by the 6th corps. But then at all times this particular document has been placed on the screen and it's not clear at what point my learned friend moves from commentary on the previous situation under the Bradina order to the situation under this order, if the witness has got anything to say about this order, if he's seen it before or if he had reason to know about it before. And there has to be clarity about that because the original hypothetical or the original scenario upon which this witness was asked to comment was that first order, the one which effectively wasn't complied with. We've now moved to something that's later in time so that has to be very clearly delineated because things can change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe Mr. Re, first of all you have to establish the relationship between the previous document and this one in clear terms. Secondly, you may come to this document, you may test the knowledge of this witness on whether he received this document before or he ever saw this document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness has already said he saw it I think 18 months ago when the Prosecution interviewed him. He didn't receive it at the time. There is no question about him receiving it at the time. The first document I was referring to was the order to send the troops to Jablanica. I'm asking him to comment in military terms on what the resubordination means. It was an introduction. I'm very confused by what my learned friend was actually putting to Your Honour. But if clarification is required, I'm very happy to assist. But I'm not quite sure what the confusion is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you have to establish a sequence of the two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I've moved from the first document, which was the one where the 2nd of September where Mr. Halilovic requested certain troops. I just moved to your evidence where you said that they were subordinated to you until they went to the Supreme Command in Jablanica and then they were within Mr. Halilovic's chain of command. So now I'm moving to this document dated the 6th of September and I'm asking you to comment on what paragraph 1 means in military terms, based upon the order Mr. Halilovic sent to you earlier, to send the troops there, your response to him, the troops going there, if they did, and what that actually means in terms of the subordination you've just given evidence about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that exposes the reason why the confusion occurred, Your Honour. Would Your Honour just look to line 15 of this -- sorry, line 14 of my learned friend's question. The question has this lengthy preamble to it explaining that -- and at that line it says that the -- Mr. Re is putting it to the witness that he says that the units were subordinated within Mr. Halilovic's chain of command. Now, he hasn't said anything like that, that they were subordinated within Mr. Halilovic's chain of command. It has yet to be established that this witness says that Mr. Halilovic had any chain of command at the moment. Now the witness has got to give the evidence step by step in a proper way and you can't have those preambles to questions particularly when they contain material that in my submission is not accurate. The witness has to be asked the questions in a step-by-step way. If he says that Mr. Halilovic has got a chain of command, that's the evidence, but it's got to be his evidence and not that coming from the Prosecutor in the style of a question. And so I maintain my objection and I point out that that's not what the witness said that's been contained in this preamble.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I understand where the confusion is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I'll quote back what the witness said,"So as" -- this is at page 26. "So as corps commander I did have command from the top down and as such I had the authority of command -- control and command over these companies up until the point in time when they arrived at their destination and reported to the Supreme Command group which was headed by General Sefer Halilovic. After that the chain of command which functioned which was established in the course of the implementation of the operation, Neretva 93 operation, this chain of command and command -- this chain of command had command and control over them." Unquote. Now, if that doesn't mean subordination, we shouldn't all be in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the Prosecutor's case. We don't think we should be in this courtroom. But that's their case. But it's no good coming from Mr. Re. It's got to come from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is this a dispute over terminology, command and control and subordination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well. I believe the witness answered this question, which is quite understandable. However, the Defence have some difficulties with this, and Mr. Re, would you please ask a very direct question to this witness, whether the troops is under the command of Mr. Halilovic when they came to that place? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You heard the question, General. Was it your understanding -- or what was your understanding of whether or not those troops were under General Halilovic's control or command and control when they were to report to Bradina or the general command -- or the Supreme Command in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance to previous documents, and in particular the order from General Sefer Halilovic which I received, I sent the units to Jablanica according to that order. They reported at Jablanica to the team, namely the team headed by General Sefer Halilovic, who was Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command. The Chief of Staff is not one to command one or two companies. Such a person at such a high post does not directly command soldiers. The corps commander either does not directly command the soldiers or the commander of the division, operational group or a brigade, because these are high functions. That is why General Sefer Halilovic wrote this order which I didn't know about during the war. I wasn't -- it wasn't of interest to me. As corps commander I was only interested in the order that I received. I sent units out in accordance with that order, in order to implement a specific task. I'm not interested in what kind of a task it is because I'm a corps commander. I have my own duties, many other duties. 75.000 soldiers, and I should not be dealing with 200 soldiers. That is why General Halilovic wrote this order, whereby units from the 1st Corps that arrived were resubordinated to the Zulfikar detachment or brigade. So that he would not be directly in command of two companies because there is no military logic to this, this is not proper, and it cannot be done that way. What the further chain of command was, and how it was established, and what it was as a whole during the course of the implementation of the Neretva-93 operation, is very difficult for me to say. I was not kept abreast of things. I found out and learned many things after the war only, when I was looking at numerous documents. This is a question that requires a much broader answer, and perhaps an expert approach to this answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was the general resubordinating?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order, which was drafted by General Sefer Halilovic, at the bottom of the document, if you can look, you can see that this order was not given to the 1st Corps command or to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is: Who was he resubordinating the 1st Corps units to -- from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Again I'm got an objection to this. If Your Honours have regard to this particular document, you will see that it's a document with a variety of purported resubordinations on it and at the bottom of it, it says in the English version that it's from Sefer Halilovic. It's dated the 6th of September in Jablanica. You'll notice that it's not signed by Sefer Halilovic. You'll also remember the evidence of Sefko Hodzic, the journalist who the Prosecution called effectively to say where Mr. Halilovic was at all times. Now, this document was not written by Halilovic and it can't be the Prosecution case that it was. Because they are saying he went with Hodzic and was away from Jablanica on the 6th. This document coming from the 6th has got the name of Halilovic there but no signature. For this witness to be asked to comment on it, as he says himself he hasn't seen it before, in this way, he's doing a bit of an unfairness to the witness, frankly, and in my submission it's doing an unfairness to the Defence without it being at least clarified on what basis he's looking at it. The witness at the moment appears to be trading this witness as a genuine good-faith document which it may be or may not be. We don't know. But at the moment it's just a document that's not signed by Sefer Halilovic and comes from Jablanica where you and the Prosecution know he wasn't. And as a result of that, Your Honours, when my learned friend puts as part of his question who was Sefer Halilovic resubordinating to, that assumes that it was Sefer Halilovic doing the resubordinating rather than some other person in Jablanica. And for those reasons, I object to that question being phrased as it was. And generally speaking I want to make this observation about the current questions: I don't object to Mr. Karavelic being given the chance to offer informed commentary on particular documents, but to mix it up with the narrative evidence is dangerous. It's after 11 years it's dangerous for a witness to be put in the position of saying, firstly what he remembers, and then secondly what his expert comment is. Now I don't object to the narrative. The Prosecution is fully entitled to get everything he remembers and everything he did and they can show him as many documents as are useful to achieve that end. I don't object. Secondly I don't object to the Prosecutor showing him documents for commentary if it's appropriate for him to comment. But it has to be clear what the dividing line is, otherwise whether we come later on, to consider what all this means, when we look at the transcript, it's going to be a mixture, and it's going to be very hard to untangle it, and it will be hard to see what use can be made of it. Of course, on the Sanction device you might get a nice, cutout bit, but to follow the whole meaning of the evidence is difficult. And frankly I'm finding it ditch myself now and that may just be my intellectual shortcomings but in my submission it's not appropriate to have mixture of narrative and expert evidence. It's apt to confuse, and it's put the witness now of dealing with this particular document, as if it's bona fides, whereas it's not proved. So that's the long speech. I understand that and I apologise for it. There is an objection to the specific but there will be other objection of this nature. So now what the people know what the Defence position is, it can be responded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage I have to remind you that this document has already been admitted into the evidence and your objections that we should bear in mind in the future stage. And as for the organisation of the direct examination, I believe that is entirely in the hands of the Prosecution. Maybe they should reorganise their questions and way of presenting their evidence at a later stage. My suggestion is that we have a short break and during which both parties will think it over, about how to deal with this witness. And we'll resume at quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. I just want to raise something very briefly in the absence of the witness. I just wish to place on the record - I didn't do it before because the witness was here - the Prosecution's objection to the type of objection my learned colleague Mr. Morrissey made before the break in which he discussed at some length the evidence of other witnesses and the authenticity or otherwise of a document which is already in evidence. In our submission it's not a proper thing to do in front of a witness and if Mr. Morrissey wishes to do it again the witness should be asked to leave the room so we can discuss this and his evidence not be contaminated. I raise this now in the hope that it doesn't recur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course, but if we engage into this kind of argument, we will spend hours or days on those issues. utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Still on the document P122, the order of the 6th of September 1993, with Mr. Halilovic's name at the bottom of it, my question is still regarding what you've described as the resubordination, and I'm asking you to comment, as a general who retired, as a brigadier general or a major general, in the Bosnian army last year -- military service and a person who has given expert testimony over several weeks in other proceedings before this Tribunal, as well as based upon your knowledge of your troops going to Herzegovina, I'm asking you to comment in -- as to the meaning you see in paragraph 1 of that order, in terms of the resubordination. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The concept of resubordination in the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and before that in the Yugoslav People's Army, and I believe in virtually any army in the world, is understood to mean the following. When a unit is resubordinated from one unit to another unit, in connection with a specific task, the moment the unit leaves and joins the other unit, and is placed under the control of that other unit, from that time, from that moment, it is to execute all the duties and obligations issued it by the new commander. Up to the time the resubordination ceases as such, i.e., until the return of that unit back to its parent unit. I should like to remark that the -- in the process of resubordination, the unit of that leaves and goes to this other unit, and is resubordinated to the other unit and the other commander. This is not to say that it is actually extracted from the organic establishment of its previous unit. That is precisely why the term "resubordination" is used. Resubordination as a rule is used for a specific, shorter period of time, a couple of days, 15 days, a month, it may be longer, for several months, but this is only very seldom. Precisely because it is very difficult to work in this way over a longer period of time, namely when you have a unit from elsewhere under your command. If such a unit is resubordinated to this other unit, and this other commander. And these are the most frequent reasons why this is resorted to only for shorter periods of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking at that document, what was happening, or what was supposed to happen to the units from the 1st Corps? Those were the units that were under your command previously.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you say that they were under my command previously. You could also say previously under the command or subordinated to Rasim Delic because that is absolutely the same thing. Because one has to properly grasp the chain of command in the army. They are not directly subordinated to me, but they are within my chain of command. And they are also in the chain of command starting from the top, starting from Rasim Delic or starting from the Supreme Command down. Item one of this order means that the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, then, resubordinated 1st Corps units in the -- to the effect of the meaning that I just explained before, to a special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How was he able to do that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has a right to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking at that order, who is the special unit subordinated to, that is the Zulfikar unit?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know to whom it is resubordinated. According to some of my sources, and having read some documents, up to that time, that unit had been an independent unit at the level of our corps, which directly reported to the Supreme Command Staff, and the -- judging by this document, according to this document, it was not resubordinated to anyone, but as I said, according to some documents which I have read, that unit, the special Zulfikar detachment, was supposed to become part of the organic establishment of the 4th Corps, if I remember correctly. Now, whether that actually took place or not, I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If Your Honour could just excuse me for one moment? Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does this document indicate that the Chief of Staff, whose name is on the document, was able to issue orders to the Zulfikar Reconnaissance Sabotage Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special detachment, the Zulfikar, directly reported to and was directly subordinated to the commander of the Supreme Command Staff, just like I myself was as the commander of the 1st Corps. It was absolutely at the same level. How much was Sefer Halilovic able to command that detachment, that depended on how much powers General Delic gave him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you comment from that order as to how much powers General Delic had given General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather not comment on that, because in this entire situation, I was subordinated to both of them, and as subordinated, I did not have the right, one in that position actually has no right to think about the -- or comment the actions of his superiors, but if this is a document that was signed by General Sefer Halilovic, and sent it to the special Zulfikar detachment, the document itself says everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably that Rasim Delic had actually invested him with the right, given him the right to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is the nature of this particular order, in military terms?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the word "order" in itself is self explanatory, I believe. An order which has the character of the grouping or forming of units, or, rather, the better term to use is the grouping of units for a forthcoming specific mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is bound by that order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is binding upon -- but first let me see to whom it is submitted, at the bottom of the page. It is binding first of all on the commander of the Zulfikar Brigade. I believe that its previous designation was "special detachment," but at that time it was renamed the Zulfikar Reconnaissance Brigade. So he was to receive these units that were being resubordinated to him, and place them under his control. Then, it was also binding on the commander of the 6th Corps, because some of these units were probably also from the organic composition of the 6th Corps as well as of the 4th Corps. Now, whether there were some units from the 4th Corps or not, or whether some combat activities were to take place in the zone of responsibility of the 4th Corps is something which I cannot explicitly infer, conclude, from the part of it which refers to the 4th Corps. Then it was also submitted to the archives and the Dreznica Battalion from the 47th Mountain Brigade. And naturally, it was also binding upon the commanders of these units from the 1st Corps that had come to the Neretva River valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can the witness please be shown the next document, which is 65 ter 171, ERN 03634076?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 385.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is a document of the 6th of September 1993, an order addressed to the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion Command which bears your name and a signature. Is that a document which was drafted at your direction, which you signed and issued?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We certainly appreciate you would have signed hundreds, thousands of documents, over the course of your -- over the course of the war and your duties as the 1st Corps commander. But just --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many more, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You say "probably yes." Why do you say "probably yes"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the fact that I see the stamp of the 1st Corps, I believe that this is my signature, and if this document was extracted from the archives of the Army of the Federation, as an official document, and did not come from some other sources, what have you, is not a forged document, then there is no reason for me to doubt the authenticity of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, is there anything in it which causes you to doubt its authenticity?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is nothing actually that I see in it that would induce me to think that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The -- look at part 1 of the record which says "assignment." It says "in cooperation with units of -- with the units of the 4th and 6th Corps, in that area, carry out offensive combat operations with the purpose of liberating the Jablanica-Mostar communication, combat activities in that area are carried out under the command of a group from the SVK led by NSRBiH, armed forces military command." Unquote. I want you to comment on that information.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Comment how? I can only read it. That's all I can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Read it first and I want you to comment upon the accuracy of the information in this order that you signed. From where did you get this information, for example?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I do not doubt the source of this document, that also means that I also confirm the entire content of the document, as I said a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's move to number 3. It says, quote "Company carries out the stated assignment not longer than seven days after the day of reporting to the SVKIKM." That's the Supreme Command staff, forward command post in Jablanica. Unquote. What was the -- what is meant by "seven days"? Why have you put "seven days" in this document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably based on an agreement with somebody that the units would stay there for a period of seven days, to implement that task.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, who was the agreement with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Sefer Halilovic, I assume, but I'm not sure. I don't remember. Or with Rasim Delic. But I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying you had communication with either Sefer Halilovic or Rasim Delic in which the period of seven days was agreed upon but you now cannot remember which one you spoke to or communicated with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was constantly in touch with General Delic and with Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which one was it more likely that you were in contact with in relation to the seven days' period agreement?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that a memory-related issue?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's addressed to the 2nd independent motorised battalion command to the attention of the commander, that's Adnan Solakovic. Do you recall discussing his assignment to liberate Jablanica-Mostar communication with him?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It's possible, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, there is. We don't -- the Defence doesn't necessarily accept the genuineness of this document here, and we can put the arguments now if you like to or we can leave it to the end. I'm not sure. We changed track on the practice we were using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have any serious objections on that or do you have any evidence pointing that it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We just have the evidence of the witnesses who -- who indicate -- the base of the objection is this: Firstly, this witness says quite clearly he doesn't remember the individual document. Well, that's fine, that's not in itself enough to be an objection. But then you have the evidence of other witnesses now - I'm not sure if this is going to occasion an objection here, but there is the basis of my objection now, so I'm going to put it before the Court - of these people from --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There will be -- there will be if it's in front of this witness. Your Honour asked me -- invited me to -- to interrupt if that was going to happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe we could defer the decision of this document to a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We could, Your Honour. There is a matter I want to raise, actually, about -- no, no, it's not appropriate to do it now. We'll do it later, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, we will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karavelic, let's go back to the document. Just have a look at the signature which is on the document. Does that appear to be your normal signature?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As corps commander, I also had a signature, what do you call it, a sort of stamp facsimile signature, a stamp. So I think that I didn't sign this by hand but used the stamp signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is also -- to the left of that there is a stamp which says IK -- well, 1st Corps, with the Bosnian coat of arms there. Is that the 1st Corps stamp?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the 1st Corps stamp, but there were two or three stamps, at least two. There should be the number 1 here, if that was my stamp. Number 2 if it was the stamp that was used at the forward command post of the corps. I don't see the number 1 here but I don't necessarily have to be right about that. I'm not sure, but I think that that is the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We can -- can the stamp area please be enlarged for the witness? We've blown it up pretty large now to cover the full screen. Does that assist you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer. I think that that is the stamp. I know that there was the stamp also bearing the number 2. I don't know if that means that this main stamp had to bear the number 1, too. I'm not sure. This was because of the forward command post. When I as corps commander set up a command post, a forward command post, it had to have its own stamp and that stamp would bear the number 2. This stamp, however, would not leave the main corps command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, this --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any doubts about that, but I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At the top of the document, there is a handwritten 333, and a 402. 402 is crossed out and there is a circled one in the top right-hand corner. Can you comment on what those numbers mean?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is also some handwriting, I think you'll find it on the back of the document, which means you'll have to go to the second page. Can you just read out what that says? Can you possibly blow it up?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read it correctly, it states here, "Sarajlic, Asmir, escort of Nihad, Bojadzic; Tahirovic, Mirsad, private."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who are those people?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of these three names, only one is known to me, Nihad Bojadzic, that's the only one I know. I don't know who the other two people are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Nihad Bojadzic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the officers who was -- I don't know at which post in the Zulfikar Brigade. I don't know whether he was in the staff of that brigade or the deputy commander of the Zulfikar Brigade. For a while, in 1993, while I was at Igman, he was in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whose handwriting that is?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is also some numbers over written above that handwriting. 0363-4076 A, then underneath that it appears to say 13B or BB, underlined. Can you comment on what they mean?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I really cannot. It doesn't signify anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
