utterances.text: It might be the Prosecution numbers, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you have objections to this document? Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, we do. I think I've already. This is still part of the first document, I think, of the original document. In other words, the order that we are critical of that we want to make a -- make a -- or raise issues about later, this writing seems to be attached to the second page to it, so it's going to be part of the objection, actually speaking, that when we come to it that -- well, I don't want to raise it now but yes that second page is just as much criticised as the first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Led wait to the later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was -- the ERN that was -- my mistake was that the"A" -- "A" actually means -- I think it means -- it's written on the reverse side of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can we please move to 65 ter number 49, which is 0219-6085?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 386.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's a document dated the 7th of September 1993, addressed to the 1st Corps Command under the hand of Adnan Solakovic, with a signature coming from the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion. Now, have you seen this document before coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it during the war. I'm not sure whether I saw it before I arrived at The Hague or whether it was once I arrived at The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the information contained there, that is about the company of 125 soldiers being sent to Jablanica at 1900 hours to execute the required tasks on the 6th of September 1993, went to the sector under the command of the Chief of Staff, is that information accurate, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult for me to say anything other than: If the document is authentic, then it's true, whatever it says in the document. This is a very small thing, so I cannot really remember anything in particular in connection with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. It's described as a daily operations report. Is that something you would have -- you would have seen in the normal course of your business as the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that the 1st Corps, amongst other things, had about 40 units linked with it. Each of those units had to -- its duty was every day, in the evening, at 1800 hours or 2000 hours, to send such a daily operative report to the 1st Corps command. All these reports were summarised at the operations centre, and they would make an overview for the corps commander. In the evening, when all the reports had arrived, the most important things would then be reported to the corps commander by the Chief of Staff. So the corps commander would not actually see most of these reports. I could even say 99 per cent of the reports, with his own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does this document appear to you, from your knowledge of the means of communication and the stationary used by the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion and the stamp and the signature and so on, does it appear to you to be a genuine document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, is there an objection to the document? If there is not an objection to the document I'll tender it. But it will take me a long time, otherwise. There is a short way and a long way of tendering these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there a reason for that question, I mean that specific question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There is an objection to the document. There will be an objection to the document. If my learned friend wishes to go through any steps he wishes to, he can. We will object to the document, that's true, but the objection wasn't about that. The objection was putting in leading information about this witness's knowledge of the stationary of the 2nd Independent Battalion. He has to prove he had some knowledge first and not assume it in the question. And that's the objection. We just ask that he go step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are going to be here for a very long time if we do this with every document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I should indicate this, we have asked for chain of custody in relation to a number of documents. In any event I'm not concerned by us being here for a long time. I just have to take objection to the question. The Tribunal can rule on it. Either I succeed or fail and then we continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's deal with one thing after another. The first thing is about the question itself. I don't believe that there is any problem for the question to put to this witness. So the -- we could not accept that objection from the Defence. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm asking you based upon your knowledge of communications within the corps and your knowledge of the 2nd independent stationary, the signature of Mr. Solakovic, the stamp on it and so on, whether it appears to you to be a genuine document.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, I have no particular objections, but I cannot verify its authenticity. I don't know off by heart the number of the military unit. It's impossible to know that. A pentium would have to memorise how many units I had in the corps and what their numbers were. It's probably correct, but if it isn't and I confirm it, then what would happen then? I cannot confirm it or deny it. And also whether this is the signature of the battalion commander. As an example, it probably is. But what if it isn't? If we are questioning that. As a witness, I would not really go into that, if I don't have to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is there anything on the face of the document to indicate whether it was sent from the 2nd Independent Motorised Brigade and received by the command of the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom of the document, it says that it was sent to the 1st Corps Command and that it was also archived in the operation centre of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion. This is most often the format used in correspondence, but I cannot claim with 100 per cent certainty whether it arrived at the command of the 1st Corps, whether a bomb fell and hit the courier or something. There is no way that I can know something like that. Excuse me, but in order to establish it, you would need to find the register books of the operations centre and the 1st Corps Command. You would need to find the record book of the operations centre of the 2nd Independent Motorised Brigade to see who took the document, how it was sent to the 1st Corps Command. You would need to find the signature of that person, whether they sent it by Paket or took it personally. This is something that you would find in the log books. It's just a mechanism. That's how the service worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Trial Chamber about the departure of these units for Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You sent some orders, you said you sent orders to at least the 2nd Independent Battalion, the 9th and 10th Mountain Brigades, to Caco and Celo to gather men to send to Herzegovina and to report to Bradina or Jablanica. How did they go? What was the mechanism? Did you see them off?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a lot in your question that needs to be clarified. I sent the orders to the unit commands, or to the commanders. They, at least I think, received clear instructions and clear tasks, based on those orders. Namely, to prepare the unit, a certain number of men, and by the time stated in the order send them to the destination, i.e. Jablanica. In what manner, which transport means to use, which route, this was all stated. In case of a delay or bad weather or something, perhaps that would change but everything else was there, and the units did leave. The reports did arrive at the 1st Corps Command once the units departed, and one of such reports is probably this one from the 2nd Independent Battalion. When I issue an order, then it is up to the brigade commander, if we are talking about a small unit, through his own chain of command, and with his officers, to regulate and make sure that the unit reaches its destination safely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just said that the reports did arrive at the 1st Corps command and one of such reports is probably this one from the 2nd Independent Battalion. Just for clarity, that is the MFI 386, the order -- sorry, the report of the 7th of September 1993 which is possibly still on the screen in front of you. Is that correct? I'm just clarifying part of your last answer. You said one of those reports. I'm just trying to tie it to a document. Are you referring to the one on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably, because that fits in; that's probably the document. But I did not see it with my own eyes at the time, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the normal process when a commander sent troops off to participate in combat? What did you personally do? I'm specifically asking you whether you personally -- was it a practice to personally address the troops?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty of all in the chain of command, including even the Supreme Command, or members of the Supreme Command, and not to mention all the other lower-ranking staff in the chain of command, is usually to appear in front of the whole unit, or a part of the unit, depending on the situation, before more serious and more important combat assignments were begun.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you appear in front of the soldiers who were going to Jablanica? Did you speak to them?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of all the soldiers and all the units that went to Jablanica, I think that I addressed the 1st unit that was sent from the 9th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact date. It was probably the day they left or the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you? Where did you address them?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were in front of the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Celo there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard to say who was there. It's possible but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What Mr. Colonel Imsirevic, do you remember whether he was there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same reply. I would give the same reply as I did on -- about the one concerning Ramiz Delalic, Celo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you say to the troops?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot repeat it word for word. It's hard, so much time later. But the gist of it was, and it was a very brief address, of perhaps five or six minutes, that it was a very serious assignment and in the way that they carried out all regular combat assignments in the 1st Corps they should, in the same way, properly and consciously implement this provisional combat assignment from -- away from the 1st Corps. That was the gist of it. It was just a brief address, the same as when other units or any other unit is sent to carry out any other combat assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you tell them where they were going?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them everything which is written in the order, which was in writing, I told them orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're referring to Mr. Halilovic's order of the 2nd of September? Which is Exhibit P38 -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that order and my own order that I had sent to the motorised brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: For the record, I meant P12 -- I'm sorry, 161. Did you tell them that they were going to be subordinated to the Zuka unit?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't even know that at the time. There was not a theoretical chance. I didn't know at the time that they would be subordinated to Zulfikar's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did you tell them they were to be subordinated to when they got there, if you did?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. He didn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you did?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The objection is that he hasn't said he told them they would be subordinated to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll just withdraw the question. I'll re-ask it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you tell them that they were to be subordinated to anyone, and if so, to whom?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the kind of conversation that a corps commander has with the men. The corps commander is also a very high post. And in such addresses, he addresses nice words to the men, in order to motivate them. And as regards this particular issue that you are referring to, this is something that the corps commander sees to through his chain of command. This is something that we should know, because this is a matter of principle, when it comes to the functioning of the military system. Of course, my written order contained all these details and my written order actually provides the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to move to -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's time for us to take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Really? Of course, of course, I'm sorry, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at quarter to one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told us earlier that you sent orders to the brigades -- I'm sorry, the units, in accordance with Mr. Halilovic's order which was P161 of 2nd of September, and we've gone through P383, which was your order of the 4th of September to Celo personally. Did Caco and Celo go to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information that they had indeed been there, down there. Whether they left at that time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Adnan Solakovic? Did you approve of his going to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. I may have. It is possible. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he go to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also think that he was there, had been there. When he went there, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To clarify something from your evidence this morning, was he a person who required your permission to leave Sarajevo and go to Herzegovina, by virtue of his position?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was customary for him and for the commander of the 9 Mountain Brigade, because they reported directly to me, yes. However, it was not always something which was strictly binding, which strictly had to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think your evidence earlier was that someone in Caco's position, as the head of a brigade, required your permission to leave Sarajevo. Did you give him permission to go to Herzegovina with parts of the 10th motorised -- sorry, Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall him asking for any permission. I do not remember that he asked me anything of the kind, and I never issued him any orders to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In military terms, what was the situation, if he left Sarajevo without your permission?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. What would it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, if your permission was required and he left without obtaining your permission, what would that mean in military terms?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be a breach of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be a shown document which is number 54 on our 65 ter list, 02196034?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 387.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There is a daily operative report from the 2nd Independent Motorised Brigade, addressed to the 1st Corps Command and the operations centre of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion, dated the 9th of September 1993. Do you recall seeing this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is the same as in reference to the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I obtain an indication from the Defence if they are objecting to this document at the moment, just to see how far I have to go with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my friend can obtain that indication. The fact is, we do object to it, and I can indicate one of the bases on which we object and that is that when Mr. Okovic was here, who is the man who is mentioned, they didn't show it to him. And trying to show it to this witness in my submission is not appropriate or proper. There are all sorts of ways I could describe it, but it's -- it really a matter of concern that when the witness, the person who actually knows about it is called and they don't ask him, to then try to slip it in through this witness, in my submission, is not appropriate and I object to its tender. I object to its use, frankly, altogether because whether the Defence is effectively -- all right. I've put it on the table. I won't advance argument now. I'll just indicate that we object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, I mean, I don't want to get into a slinging match about, quote, "trying to slip it under the -- slip it through this witness," unquote. If it wasn't put to Mr. Okovic, I don't know, I didn't take the witness. I'm not in a position to comment on that. But I'm entitled to show the witness a document which appears in the normal course of it to be one addressed to his corps command. I might be able to address the Court later on why it wasn't shown to Mr. Okovic. Maybe we just forgot to. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that using of this document is allowed and the objections from the Defence is partially denied. But as for whether we admit it into the evidence or not, I believe that we could only make the ruling after some questions put to this witness by the Prosecution. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic -- excuse me. All right. You answered earlier that -- I think your answer -- the earlier answer means that you don't recall seeing this in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that I had -- that I said sorry in connection with the previous document also applies to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What can you say about looking at the document, what sort of document it is, and whether it appears to you to be a genuine document issued from the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll put it on record again. Again I object to this. It seems to be an attempt to authenticate the document and give the document some sort of weight when he's given his clear indication as to whether he's ever seen it before. So it can't be done. Your Honours, I don't object, and I've made this clear in the past, that the witness can be asked about things he knows about. If he knows about the information here, that could assist the Tribunal. But if he doesn't know about, it won't. And I don't object to questions like that. But an attempt to make the document look real when effectively the Prosecution aren't proving that it's real is not permissible, and that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe there witness has already said that he did not see this document in 1993. It's very difficult for this witness to say it's a genuine document or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In -- all right. As the corps commander, he must be entitled to comment upon whether a document -- whether a document which is issued or -- sorry, which is issued from subordinate unit within his command, which is addressed to his corps command, bears the indicia of authenticity based upon his experience as the corps commander and seeing documents of this type. I mean -- I mean, that's as far as I can take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it seems to me that you are going to ask this witness to make a conclusion on this document, but I believe that you're entitled to ask the general question. For instance, whether this document is within the format of the normal orders within his commander, and whether this witness is familiar with whatever is said in this document, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: General, this document, does it appear to -- well, is it within the format of normal communications within the 1st Corps in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There exist a multitude of different types of documents. It goes without saying that this document is one of the documents that can be categorised as falling under one of these many forms of documents. There had been similar documents, that much I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does it appear to be on 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion letterhead?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no person that could confirm that or say anything substantiated in connection with that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could understand your question, you're asking me about the type of paper and whether the document was authentic in terms of the manner of writing and the type of paper and the document as shown to me on the monitor. So if I can say this, it is not an appropriate question to me. In order for me to be able to reply to such a question I would have to have the original document in my hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Unfortunately we don't have the original here but I can show you a paper copy, if that might assist you. If it is easier to read it, I can certainly show you -- show it to you on a piece of paper. Would that help?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I doubt it. I doubt that that would be of any significant help in order for me to be more clear or more precise in my response.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Look, if you look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you possibly blow up the logos in the top left-hand corner, please? To the left, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There are two -- two logos there, one is the army and the other one, to the left, is that the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion's logo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say one thing, which is true. I have seen this only very seldom, and I'm not quite clear as to what this particular logo is. It is stated on the document itself, first of all, under tool, on the top is 2nd, 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion and then the 1st Corps of the Army of B and H. This is totally contrary to the rules of drafting documents. This is not the way this is done. So my conclusion is that this was done by an incompetent officer. Now, what this logo on the left means, stands for, is something that I cannot say anything about. It doesn't ring any bells, as far as I'm concerned. But it is on the document. That I can see, of course. This is very rare. This is perhaps a unique example that you have, this order of units on the letterhead. I mean, of a thousand documents, perhaps you will find one or none that look like that. I guarantee you that. Of course, you can gain access to the archives of the 1st Corps and its command in the federal archives and you can be satisfied of that for yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the army logo to the right of that? Is that the normal army logo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logo to the right is a symbol which was quite customary and was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the stamp at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the stamps -- or, rather, the army had two types of stamp. The first type of stamp was like this, with a coat of arms of Bosnia and Herzegovina inscribed in it, but also with the full designation of the unit in question. That was one kind of stamp. And this stamp that you see now, that is a second, a different, type of stamp. The stamp is of the same size. Inscribed in it is the coat of arms of Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it only designates the unit and the number of the unit, and the commander actually assigns numbers to all units by a special directive. And this is something that is hard for one to know by heart. It is in fact impossible. So probably this number, which is there, is the secret number, the secret designation, on the stamp of the 2nd Independent Battalion, but this is only a supposition on my part. That is, if I do not doubt the document. And that of course doesn't have to be the case, as far as the doubting of it is concerned, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. The numbers, are they 5438?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think so. I guess it is 5438. I cannot be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're saying that you can't remember now but that may have been the designation of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each unit had a numerical designation of this kind. Absolutely each and every unit had to have such a numerical designation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And Mr. Sakib Okovic, do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was an officer in the command of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with his signature?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just raise a matter there. Perhaps I should have objected to that question a bit quicker. The answer didn't -- or, the answer happened in any event, but there was somebody here who might have answered the question as to the signature. And there is a question in any event as to whether this particular Okovic here is the same person who came. But the Okovic who came is the person who was -- who we know played a role down in Herzegovina, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't understand. Is Mr. Morrissey saying that it's a different Mr. Okovic? I'm not sure what he's saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Actually, the witness has answered that question already, so -- well, I believe that Mr. Morrissey just wants to register his objections in the transcript on that particular matter. On that issue, I believe that the author himself is the best person to recognise his own signature. On this part, I agree with Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think the witness -- I think it was a different witness. I think it was that a Mr. Zakija Okovic [phoen], not a Mr. Sakib Okovic. I think there is two. There may be two different people. I'll have to check this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But shall we proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The original objection was that Mr. Okovic had actually testified here, and he was the guy who should be authenticating. That was the original objection. I think we might be on different levels here. That's why I was confused before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said earlier that -- I'm just trying to find the passage it was some minutes ago, you mentioned the competence it must have been drafted by someone who was incompetent because the way the logos were there or something to that effect. Are you making a comment on Mr. Okovic's competence, by that answer?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whoever is the author of the signature, whoever is the signatory, yes, that is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What about the -- I want to ask you about the information in the document. Are you familiar with the information in the document, about the order issued by the chief of the Supreme Command headquarters, two couriers returning to the base, it was written in the order we should find and deliver communications equipment, and then the list of -- list -- 19 specific pieces or types of equipment are listed.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Moving from that document, what communications, if any, did you receive from the units who went to Herzegovina after they went there? That's the 9th, the 10th, the 2nd Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours there is just one matter that arises from the previous passage of cross-examination that should really be clarified here. This witness indicated that he knew and was familiar with a particular person. Now that being the person who's named there, Sakib Okovic, and that it ought to be clarified since the Prosecutors have called another individual at a senior level, with the name of Zakir Okovic, which one he knew, whether he knew Zakir Okovic the witness in this case, Sakib Okovic, the person whose name appears on that document, whether they are the same person in fact or whether they are two different people. Now, I can ask it in cross-examination, of course, but because the issue is now live, it's a matter that's arisen and there has been -- expressed some doubt about it on the Prosecution side in my submission that ought to be asked before we leave that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, do you mind asking this question to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. I don't. I just need a copy of Mr. -- what's his name? The other one. The one who gave evidence. I just need a copy of his statement to get his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Zakir, Z-a-k-i-r, and "Okovic" is spelled the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just need a copy of his statement to get the personal details to put them to the witness. It may just take a moment to find. If I can return to that later -- I will get back to it but I just can't do it right at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was my question. I've lost it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you receive from the units who went to Herzegovina after they went there, that's the 9th, 10th and the 2nd Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's my question.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific in putting that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. At -- on Mr. Halilovic's orders you dispatched, at least three sets of soldiers under your command or from your corps to Mr. Halilovic. After they went -- after they got there, did you receive reports back from them? Or any form of communication?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember having received any reports. I'm not aware of any such reports. And I did not maintain any contact with my units until the time they returned. Of all the contacts that I do remember, or reports, there was just this one report by the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion, Adnan Solakovic, when once he spoke to me via a Motorola and we had a very brief conversation, lasting perhaps one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was it about?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He actually asked to talk to me. It was not I who talked to him. And basically, he requested me that he be withdrawn from down there and returned to the corps as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did he want to be withdrawn? What did he say to you about the reason?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't give any reasons. He just said something to the effect that the situation was serious, that it was confusing, and nothing else. I think that at one point, that his unit is a bit specific and so on. That's what he managed to say at the time. Nothing else in particular. And I replied that I would see, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you said his unit "is a bit specific and so on." I don't quite understand what you mean by "a bit specific"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't mean anything by it. It was he who meant something by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long after -- sorry. How long after their arrival in Herzegovina did he contact you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I would need to see the document to see when he left and then when he called me, but I think it's a question of four or five, six days, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown P272?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the document there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the document that you wanted to refer to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't thinking of any particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said "I would need to see the document to see when he left and then when he called me but I think it's a question of four, five or six days." All right. Well, have a look at that document, which is addressed to you. It's dated the 11th of September 1993. Is that about the same time, which accords with your memory of when he called you; that is, four, five or six days after he arrived?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I doubt that this document was sent to me. When you say that this document was sent to me as the commander of the 1st Corps, this is said by the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion, Adnan Solakovic, most probably. This document that you see on the screen right now does not exist in the archives of the army of the federation or in the archives of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion, because I looked for it. Which means that the document was never sent to the 1st Corps command, this document that's being shown right now. Actually, a copy of it was given to me by the commander of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion, Adnan Solakovic. I think also at that time or very close to the time when I was signing a report with your people in Sarajevo, and I think this was perhaps a year and a half or a year ago. This was the third report. That was the first time that I saw this document, as it is. I don't know whether my conversation via the Motorola with him coincides with this document. I really don't know. I don't know when I spoke to him. I can't really rule it out, but I can't confirm it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the information in that document? Did he convey that information to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said more or less what he told me when he called me in this brief conversation. Here, if you have the translation, it states -- actually, this document was something that he had with him as a personal, private document. If you need it, I can read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Sorry, read what out?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If necessary, I can read the document out.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, no, no. We have a translation here. What I'm asking you is about the information in that. Does that assist your recollection of anything that Mr. Solakovic told you when he communicated with you by Motorola?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, I've got to object to that. This one sounds a bit technical but you can't refresh a witness's memory from something that he didn't make or didn't see. He can comment on the information in it, he can say what he remembers, but he's not to be asked to refresh his memory from something that he didn't make.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is just absolutely incorrect under common law, civil law, or any legal system. A witness can refresh his memory from anything which assists to refresh his memory. In America, they classically say they could refresh your memory from a banana. It doesn't have to be your own banana from which you can refresh your memory. It's something which is contemporaneous or which may not even be contemporaneous, which may assist to revive or refresh a memory. It doesn't matter whether it's his document or another one. Someone else could have made a record of a conversation which he took part in, and looking at the document which someone else made to assist the recollection. So the objection is just wrong in law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that a witness testified that he received a call through the Motorola at that time, from that person, and you may ask this witness whether the contents, in the conversation through that Motorola, is corresponding to the contents in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think I asked that before. I'll ask it again. I don't think I quite got an answer to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you heard His Honour's question which I sort of asked you before. Does what is written there accord in any way with what Mr. Solakovic said to you in his conversation by Motorola?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already answered that question earlier, when I said briefly what was talked about. If you read the contents of this document, then you can see the parts that correspond with the things that we talked about via the Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which parts of the document are those? Okay. I'll take you through it. "We arrived in Jablanica as it was ordered." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "We carried out reconnaissance for three days but it seems that the agreement with the chief is off."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "The operation is being postponed more and more."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a part of this was in this conversation, a small part, in a different form and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "We have the order until Sunday but it seems that it is off."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same answer applies as the previous answer relating to the previous part.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Strange things are happening." Did he say that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also via the Motorola, that was the conversation. The conversation between us was not coded. It was an open conversation. So these words were not used. But, however, in some form, he might have intimated some of this, but I cannot state that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "I am afraid for my soldiers who are of a different religion."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also perhaps in a different form. When I said that word before, because of the specificity of his unit, that would correspond with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Panic appeared in the unit."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether that word was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "People are simply disappearing overnight."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, too, is something that's very clear and quite emphatic. So it's possible that in a different form, it would correspond to the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Send us back into the town any way you can."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's more or less what I said when I summarised my conversation with him, that that was what he requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "If it is necessary, go to the head."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Let him make up a reason for the return."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would give the same answer as my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "All in all, regular."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would repeat the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "The chief put us under the command of Zuka."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "I'm afraid that a conflict between us might occur which is most probable."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's perhaps possible that I remember something vaguely, but it's not possible to remember exactly whether any of it was mentioned in the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Do that as soon as possible."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that something like that was said, because this is something that he was asking for, amongst other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "I do not want to take part in these dirty games and it is not as you were told."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that a small part of that was said in a different way, but not so directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "I will tell you all about the danger when I return."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "PS, nobody should know this."

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: "Regards, or greetings, Adnan. Reply." Sorry, just disregard the last one. There was something written over the translation. Now, what I want to ask you was -- you had that conversation with Mr. Solakovic by Motorola. What did you do when he contacted you and said that he wanted to return to Sarajevo with his troops?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Before that -- sorry, Your Honour, just before that is answered, the last part that was read out was greetings from Adnan, Zakir, and Pezo, and that should be made clear given the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's the nickname?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Zakir is a name that's on that list and evidence was given by -- by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe you have to ask that question, whether this was the nickname or the full name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking him is whether the information in the document is the same as what he said on the phone. I very much doubt that the greetings at the end would have been said in a telephone call because this is a written correspondence. That's why I didn't go to the last line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The point is not that. The point is we have to make sure they are the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I've just -- I have a real difficulty because I have "unrevised" written across the bottom line and I was asking our case manager to interpret for me what was written underneath. I don't have it in English, those last few words. If Mr. Morrissey has a translation that he could read onto the record I would be very happy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it's just what's on the screen. Your Honours, greetings from Adnan, Zakir, Pezo, and then it has the word "response" written after that. So it's really the names that there that I was asking ought to be clarified, Adnan, Zakir, and Pezo. As my friend did see fit to put the Adnan part of it, the whole lot should be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's not a matter of seeing fit. It was a matter of what I could read and I got to the point where it was no longer relevant for my --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Not suggesting cheating. Sorry, just -- I don't want to seem like I'm suggesting something mean I'm just asking that the whole lot be put. Relax.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the screen, you can see Pradrav [phoen], Adnan, Zakir, Pezo; correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Who is that Pezo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is Pezo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also one of the officers at the command of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion, the same as Zakir Okovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, what was your response to Mr. Solakovic's request of you to return to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall anything in particular. I don't think that I had any specific response. I think that later, I don't know when, whether it was the same day, in the next day, in a couple of days, I got in touch with Rasim Delic or Sefer Halilovic. I don't remember. It's possible. I cannot confirm that, when I requested the return and so on and so forth. I have some idea that perhaps I received some information from somewhere that everything was all right. Nothing else. What else could I do?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you have ordered Adnan Solakovic to return to Sarajevo without the permission of Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I could have done, but that would be a gross breach of discipline, and of the lines of subordination within the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we please move to Exhibit D273?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, this is a document dated the 11th of September 1993, headed order to attack and bears the name and the signature of Alispago, Zulfikar. Do you have the document there?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you seen this document before you were asked to testify in these proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw this document only when I came to The Hague, now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to comment in military terms upon a specific part this document. First of all, I just want your general comment on the type or the nature of document. Is it a combat order or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a heading like this, "combat order," this is then an order to embark on combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what does it tell you about the subordination of the units named in the order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you mean, what does it tell me?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, from reading this document, as a general, or a former general, in the Bosnian army, what does it tell you about the subordination of the units named and who were they subordinated to? That sort of thing.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A document like this, when it's issued, and like it says here, on this document, "combat order," everything that is stated in such a document, it's final, it's binding. The units carry out final preparations and then, under the item, "scheduling the start of the attack," by that time all the units which are under the command of the person who issues this order have to carry out the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The document names or refers to, under the heading, "axis one," and some directions, ABC, it refers, it says, "the above 60 to 80 men who shall be brought in additional are members of Adnan Solakovic's unit." Next paragraph says "the remaining 20 to 40 soldiers from the same unit (Adnan Solakovic's), shall be deployed on the right wing of this axis from Draga, (TT 5500.5) towards Vratca (TT 628)." Is that on your screen, the entire passage? Or do you need the page moved?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think it's on the first page in the B/C/S, which should be -- I apologise, which should be on page 2 and 3 of the English. The first part is on page 2 and then the specific reference is on page 3, the first paragraph. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have Your Honours seen the right passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, what does that tell you, having said it's a -- it's a final, binding combat order, what does that tell you about the subordination of Adnan Solakovic's unit when this combat attack was order -- order was issued? And I'm asking you this in your expertise as a general in the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It tells me that the person who issued this combat order, everything that's stated in this order, all the units that are mentioned in this order should and must act in accordance with this order and its elements and the times stated therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I want you to be specific about this. The document is signed or purports to be signed by Alispago, Zulfikar and has his name written on the end of it. And it refers to Adnan Solakovic's unit which was from the 1st Corps. What does that tell you about the subordination of Adnan Solakovic's unit at the point when that order was issued? Who were they subordinated -- who was his unit subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As per this document, which probably is derived from the document in which all the units of the 1st Corps are resubordinated to the Zulfikar unit, as per orders of General Halilovic, and so it means that the unit of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion was resubordinated to the unit of Zulfikar Alispago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that -- is that time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will make a break. And we'll resume at 3.30 in the same courtroom. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.44 p.m. --- Upon resuming at 3.32 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and I just got informed before the start of this afternoon's session that the Prosecution is not ready for the reply to the motions for judicial notice filed on the 1st of March 2005. So we rescheduled that short hearing tomorrow morning before we hear the witness. Is that agreeable, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that you have something to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's just two things, Your Honour. The first one was that just basically a personal matter of mine, that I just in the last couple of days have come down with a virus and, frankly, I notice myself becoming a little short tempered this morning and I just want to apologise to the Court and to my learned friend Mr. Re for showing a bit of grumpiness and grouchiness in court. It really wasn't my intention to be like that and I can say that I've got an excuse but it's not really much of an excuse. At all events, Your Honours, I only see fit to mention the illness side of things because of the tight schedule that we've got here. At this stage I'm fine to go ahead and I mean to but I've got to go and get some medical advice about this situation. But however, we are pressing on now, I'll advise the Court if there is any troubles. Things should be fine. The second matter I wanted to raise was simply that about the expert situation, that my learned friend Mr. Weiner mentioned that the expert report was awaiting the conclusion of this particular witness. Now, I'm not sure what the time lines are going to be, we have to give some thought to it, and what I would ask is that we have a discussion about this topic at the close of proceedings tomorrow because -- I mean, there is no use jumping in right now, my learned friend is taking a witness. But we do need to have some sort of time line set for that because whether or not the Prosecution chooses to get an expert at all or how that's going to proceed is a matter of interest and concern to the Defence. So we just want to know what their plans are and perhaps they could tell us that tomorrow evening and then we can make our plans, too, because we would like to use the break. It's a break that's forced on us by scheduling things, but both sides could probably use that break constructively, but experts require preparation. And in a case like this now, it might require us to consult our own experts or get a new expert involved in the case as well. In the past we have mentioned that Brigadier Dzambasovic who is a team member is likely to be called and give some evidence. And that remains the position. But at the same time we might also seek to get somebody who is an entirely outside of the proceedings, and Mr. Dzambasovic, of course, is a team member here so -- sorry, Your Honours. Anyway those are some of the reasons why we would like to have an idea of really where that's all headed. I don't call on my friend to answer it now and I'm not -- I don't make any point now, really, just having to say we should discuss this matter tomorrow because otherwise, time will slip by and we won't be able to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, this Bench is also worried about time schedule issues, especially concerning with the present witness. Mr. Re, would you please shed some light on how long you're going to still need for this present witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it's very hard to estimate. My original estimate was up to two days to complete his testimony, showing him the documents, but progress has been much slower than we had hoped or anticipated. I will go into tomorrow on present indications, on present pace. The areas I need to continue covering are the documents with Neretva, the return of the soldiers, the witness's involvement in Trebevic, in relation to the 9th and the 10th and the attempts to bring them under control, and the relationship between those brigades and Mr. Halilovic. Those are the -- I think the four discrete topics and of course I'll ask him to comment on his military expertise and the inspection team order and the map. Now, if I can get short, precise answers I could finish in the afternoon but I -- I'm not as hopeful as I was before we started. So I definitely will go -- on present pace we will go into tomorrow. In relation to the expert report, I can very briefly answer. Nothing has changed since Mr. Weiner addressed the other day. We were awaiting the finalisation of there witness's evidence before we make a final decision as to whether we get General Ridgeway to supplement his report by, in effect, doing a new report. We can't do that until the completion of the witness's evidence, which of course includes cross-examination. When that happens we will make a decision and probably travel to London to see the general and that will be over the break, and if we do it we will produce something, in time for the Defence to have time to assess it. It won't be -- it won't be a lengthy document. It certainly won't be -- there won't be any surprises in it. It will just be a reassessment in light of the different material which we provide the general with this time, which has clearly changed since the material that was provided to him some years ago because the witnesses weren't called. Clearly we have to give him different material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for this present witness, how many sittings or how many sessions do you still need? I want to -- more or less, you know, specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, my wish list wouldn't be any more at all but I think realistically, there is an hour and a half today and -- tomorrow morning. I really sincerely hope I can finish in the first session tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Morrissey? Are there lengthy cross-examination for this witness? And would you mind telling us approximately how long are you going to take?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To be specific, how many sittings, how many sessions do you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I had in mind originally two normal days. I'm not sure how things are going to play out here. I thought I needed two normal days and we've prepared pretty thoroughly, we hope, so that's to be -- that's still to be attempted. Frankly, I think it's desirable, I fully agree with the Tribunal's position about this. We should try to finish him. It's very bad when a witness gets divided by a big break. It's not fair on the witness, frankly, and it has all sorts of problems. I don't know how late people can sit, I don't know what court staff attitude is or the Tribunal's attitude is. I think it's appropriate to do everything we can, and if that means sitting longer, well, we'll cooperate with that. But I think -- I have to responsibly say that even before my learned friend commenced, I thought about two days of normal sittings, and now, I have to say that he's been asked to offer some comments on documents that I -- they were on the list there but they have taken quite a considerable amount of time. Now, how that proceeds I just don't know. I was perhaps caught wrong footed a little bit there. What I'm saying is I don't think we are doomed yet and I think it's worth continuing to try hard and I would aim myself to finish with in that two days' period. We've got a bit of extra time tomorrow so it may be, if my -- if my learned friend is able to get through what he needs to get through by tomorrow morning, we can do it and I think we should try. That's my submission, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any solutions if the worst scenario happened? Because on Friday afternoon, we did not book any sittings. I don't know at this moment whether any courtroom is free Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I think we would need one, if we could. Your Honours, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't know whether anybody of you made any travelling plans --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- next Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I did. In fact what has sustained me through this last couple of weeks is -- frankly was that fact. Your Honours, look, you know, we'll fit in. I was to be with my -- there are personal details that don't matter, I suppose. You know, obviously, but I have made a plan and I was going to fly away on Saturday morning and come back in the middle of next week and then resume work. That was my idea and I've -- we've arranged all of that. Your Honours, if it has to be that we are interposed at sometime next week, well, we'll just abide by what the Court says. What I'd be reluctant is -- I don't want -- the only thing I'd prefer is that -- I think the best thing to do is be brave and strong and just try. That's the only thing I can think of, Your Honour, and we will do everything we can to be -- be brief. That's what I'll try to do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the Bench, I believe this bench is brief enough to sit morning and afternoon for the week. Well, but anyway, we will try our best. Yes. Having said that, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll undertake that there should be no squabbles between myself and Mr. Re in the course of -- of -- of the rest of this witness, and that will speed things up too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can we please move to the next document. That will be 65 ter number 59, 01831486.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 388.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You see the document there, General?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The document has your name on it. I'm only interested in the top part of the document. It's dated the 12th of September 1993 and is addressed to the Supreme Court -- sorry, Supreme Command staff, the chief of the staff, attention Sefer Halilovic in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document I think is the one that's got two parts to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It is. That's why I said I'm only interested in the top part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, it's just that in the Bosnian version there's -- it's not just one document. It's two. Anyway, perhaps the witness can comment about that, I don't know, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only interested in the top half, the one that's got your name on it. Do you see it there, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, is that a document you sent to Mr. Halilovic on the 12th of September at about 0100 hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll just have -- the term "document" is going to have to be clarified here because the original, I don't know -- Your Honours will have the English on the screen but the original that we have has -- has got two parts to it. It's got a part on the top and a part on the bottom, and if my friend is asking him whether he sent this document, that's -- that's what probably -- then that had better be clarified. If it's not this document that he's talking about then he better say did you send some other version or some part of -- what's on the -- to use the term document -- I'm not suggesting it's deliberately misleading, but it could be confuse because a document usually refers to the original document. And that, what we have here -- I don't know -- is -- if it -- perhaps it is the original. But it better be clarified, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think, the document is used by the Prosecution is just a general term which means that it might be a paper evidence. So I believe as for the second half, the Prosecution will ask the witness to make some clarification on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Still concentrating on the top part of the document, that is the piece of paper which has been electronically transmitted to you on the computer screen, and the part which bears your signature, not the order below, which isn't yours, is the top half of that -- is the information -- can -- look, there are two documents there, one of yours and one of someone else's?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first document is mine, and part of the second document on this same sheet which was probably pasted on to the same sheet by mistake and only part of the second document was reproduced but the entire document must be in the archives of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said it's your document. Is it one that was according to that stamp sent to Mr. Halilovic on the 12th of September 1993 at 1 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It starts off by saying, "The Chief of Staff of the 6th corps informed me about a decision made by the Chief of the Supreme Command Staff regarding" -- I'm sorry. I apologise, I've got the wrong one. Start again. It says, "One, based on collected intelligence regarding the aggressor activities in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps, I'm asking you, sir [chief], to respect the orders and if possible to somehow ensure the return of parts of the 2nd Independent Battalion, the 9th Motorised Brigade and the 10th Mountain Brigade on the 12th/13th of September 1993." Now, what was the collected intelligence -- I withdraw that. Why were you asking Mr. Halilovic to respect orders? What orders were you asking him to respect?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a reference to my orders saying that the units should remain in the Neretva River valley for seven days. It is probable that this date roughly coincides with the expiry of that time period. On account of such intelligence as was gathered regarding enemy activity around Sarajevo, the aggressor's activity around Sarajevo, I was requesting that pursuant to that, the Chief of Staff return the units to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, you say, "If you still need the assistance of the parts of the aforementioned units, then I am asking you to enable the company from the 2nd Independent Battalion headed by Commander Adnan Solakovic to return to Sarajevo." Why did you say in that request that you were -- if the units had to remain there, could I please have back Adnan Solakovic's? Why did you want his back instead of the other two?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted him back for a fundamental military reason. The 2nd Independent Battalion was a mobile unit in my corps that was in the reserve. It had no area of responsibility and it was not in charge of any section of the defence line. There was information that there might be a new attack against Sarajevo by the aggressor. This was a mobile unit in reserve and it was badly needed to carry out any acts of intervention. That was probably the chief reason. We have spoken about those previous documents, and the interviews with Adnan Solakovic. That may also have to do with the call that Adnan Solakovic made to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your preference for Adnan Solakovic's unit as opposed to Celo's or Caco's men? Having them come back to Sarajevo? Why did you prefer Solakovic to bring his men back in preference to Celo or Caco?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered a minute ago. This was a mobile unit, a reserve unit. That's why. The other two units were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you contact Mr. Halilovic in relation to this request? Did you have any communication with him about this?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Halilovic, to your recollection, respond to this request?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry for that. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I move to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, there is, Your Honour. But the witness has identified it. He hasn't been asked, he's effectively said that was his, but he hasn't really provided a basis for whether he means it or not or whether it's just something that looks like -- like what he did. The document itself is unusual. I have to say, Your Honour, it's the sort of document that this objection would have to be treated a bit more weakly than some of the other ones because he's indicated -- he hasn't said anything about it at all. Perhaps I'll object at this stage now. Perhaps if my learned friend asks the question whether he remembers it and so on then I'll know what the objection is. At the moment it doesn't look as if -- we are all a bit in the dark about it. So I do object but my friend might be able to knock that on the head, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To me, it's quite clear. This document was a witness document he sent to Mr. Halilovic and he testified about the situation on that part. So I have no problem on this document, so I believe that at least the upper part of this document is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the lower part, well, I don't believe that Mr. Re tendered the lower part also into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Unless we could establish connections between the lower part and the upper part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I understand your ruling. I'm bound by the ruling. I just have to make this comment generally so I'm not seeming to be fussy about it. In a command responsibility case, of course the Prosecution is going to tender many, many documents that Mr. Halilovic may or may not have seen. That's natural. But it means I have to be particularly cautious to protect his rights because I can't have instructions on -- there are some documents that I can't, some obviously I can. Some we are going to disagree about. But I have to be very cautious about that because the chain of custody issue and the normal way of proving a document is very important in a case like this where it's command responsibility and where it can't be inferred that Mr. Halilovic himself will have seen it. And that's the reason I'm very hypersensitive, of course, about the document. It's got two documents on it, like that. Particularly when the document at the bottom is one that we have expressed our suspicions about and are intending to cast aspersions on whenever we -- whenever it gets mentioned. But I understand Your Honour's ruling, we are bound by it, so I say no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This document is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P388.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Prosecution -- sorry, Defence Exhibit D157?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, have a look at the document which is dated the 12th of September 1993 and bears the name of commander Rasim Delic at the bottom and it's addressed to the forward command post in Jablanica and the command of the 6th Corps. When did you first see this document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it during the war. It must have been at a more recent time, perhaps just before I arrived in The Hague, just after I arrived. I think it was following my arrival that I saw this document. This is the document that constitutes the lower half of the document you've just shown me, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Quite correct, yes. This one is different in that it actually has stamps on it, whereas the one that was attached to the one I showed you before appears to be an archived copy of some sort or there may be some other explanation. Now, what I want you to comment on is paragraph 2, which is "Check the accuracy of information regarding the genocide committed against the civilian population by the members of the 1st Corps, 9th Mountain Brigade; if the information is correct, isolate perpetrators and take energetic measures, do everything to prevent such actions. Order the 1st Corps 9th Motorised Brigade deputy commander to return to Sarajevo immediately in order to solve problems in the unit." Unquote. Now, were you given information at that time about a "genocide" or any atrocities at all committed against the civilian population by members of the 1st Corps, 9th Brigade? When I say "at that time," I mean on the 12th of September or very close to that period.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know when Caco, who is the deputy commander of the 9th Brigade, returned to Sarajevo? I'm sorry, Celo -- I meant -- I said Caco.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not him personally, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When were you first -- when did you first hear about what happened in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much later, following the return of my units from the Neretva River valley. You're asking me when I first heard about what happened in Grabovica. What does that mean? When did I first hear about that? Does that mean when I first heard about 1 per cent of the total information or when I heard 50 per cent of the total information or 100 per cent of the total information? Which of these are you referring to when you're asking me when I first heard about what had occurred in Grabovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, let's start with day 1. What is your memory of the first time that you were told that there had been an incident in Grabovica involving civilians?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps on the eve of the Trebevic operation, or just after the operation. There were rumours to the effect that something bad had happened during the Neretva-93 operation, or, rather, the combat activity in the Neretva River valley. Then word spread that certain civilians had been killed, Croatian civilians and so on and so forth. I have heard nothing official to this very day, but I learned about it and I heard about it once this case started to be tried by this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did Adnan Solakovic return from Herzegovina? Was it before Operation Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said earlier, before the break, that he had telephoned you -- sorry, called you by Motorola and expressed some concerns about remaining in Herzegovina and he wanted to be returned. Upon his return, did you discuss with him his concerns about why he wished to be returned from Sarajevo -- from Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he returned right away. He returned much later. I'm not sure about the day. We should go back and look at the documents. I don't remember having talked to him or indeed that he filed a written report in relation to that.
